rel-subject-scope.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a requirement in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` plan, change, or depend on the behaviour or component that `anchor.statement` governs, or an area named in `anchor.scope`? Judge subject overlap only. Do not judge whether the item obeys, carries out, or breaks the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the behaviour the anchor statement governs or on an area named in anchor.scope, whether or not it mentions or follows the anchor's rule.
criteria.no: The item concerns a different component or activity; completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell which component or behaviour it touches.

rel-reviewer-need.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor (`anchor.statement`, `anchor.scope`). Would someone checking that the plan honours `anchor.statement` need to read this item, because the item builds, changes, or relies on the behaviour, component, or queue the anchor is about, as listed in `anchor.scope`? Judge subject overlap only, not compliance.

criteria.yes: The item builds, changes, or relies on something named in anchor.statement or anchor.scope, so a reviewer of this anchor must read it, even if the item ignores or breaks the anchor.
criteria.no: The item is about an unrelated part of the system; a reviewer of this anchor could skip it.
criteria.unclear: The item text does not say enough to tell what part of the system it touches.

rel-scope-match.instructions: Compare `item.text` against `anchor.scope`, which lists the kinds of work this anchor governs, and against the subject of `anchor.statement`. Does the item do, or depend on, at least one kind of work listed there? An item that touches the subject while ignoring or contradicting the rule still matches. Judge subject match only.

criteria.yes: At least one piece of work in the item falls under anchor.scope or the subject of anchor.statement.
criteria.no: No piece of work in the item falls under anchor.scope or the subject of anchor.statement.
criteria.unclear: The item is too vague to tell whether any of its work falls under anchor.scope.

add-concrete-action.instructions: `anchor.statement` gives a concrete rule: an action that must happen, the conditions that trigger it, and any limit or default. Does `item.text` state that rule's action together with its limit or default, in its own words or the statement's, as something the item will do? A mention of the topic, a promise to 'handle' it gracefully, or a goal without the concrete action does not count. Judge whether the rule's content is present only, not whether anything else in the item conflicts with it.

criteria.yes: The item states the anchor's required action and its limit or default as part of the plan.
criteria.no: The item is silent on the rule, names only its topic or a vague intent, or plans a different action than the one the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: The item states some of the rule's concrete content, but it cannot be told whether the required action itself is planned.

add-two-step.instructions: First, identify the action `anchor.statement` requires and the limit it puts on that action. Then check `item.text`: does it commit to performing that same action within that limit? Generic wording about the topic (for example 'handle errors', 'be resilient') is not a commitment. Judge only whether the commitment is present; do not judge conflict.

criteria.yes: item.text explicitly commits to the action the statement requires, with the statement's limit or default.
criteria.no: item.text makes no such commitment: it is silent, only names the topic, or commits to some other behaviour instead.
criteria.unclear: item.text points at the required action but too loosely to tell whether it commits to it.

add-step-present.instructions: Does `item.text` contain an explicit step, constraint, or design decision that performs the behaviour `anchor.statement` requires, including the limit or default the statement sets? Count only specific content; an item that merely mentions the same subject, or that does something else instead, does not carry the requirement. Judge presence only.

criteria.yes: An explicit step or constraint in the item performs the required behaviour with the statement's limit or default.
criteria.no: No step or constraint in the item performs the required behaviour; the item is silent, topical only, or does something else.
criteria.unclear: A step in the item may perform the required behaviour, but its wording is too loose to tell.

con-cannot-coexist.instructions: Does `item.text` commit to a behaviour, limit, or default that cannot coexist with `anchor.statement`: doing the opposite of what it requires, refusing or skipping the required action in a case the statement covers, or fixing a value the statement says must differ or be configurable? Silence, vagueness, missing detail, or rules about cases the statement does not cover are not conflicts. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item commits to something that breaks the statement in at least one case the statement covers.
criteria.no: Nothing the item commits to breaks the statement, whether or not the item mentions it.
criteria.unclear: An item commitment might break the statement, but its wording is too ambiguous to tell.

con-implement-exactly.instructions: Imagine a developer implements exactly what `item.text` says. Would the result necessarily violate `anchor.statement` in at least one situation that the statement covers? An item that says nothing about the statement's subject, or that only leaves details open, would not necessarily violate it. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: Implementing the item as written would necessarily violate the statement in a covered situation.
criteria.no: Implementing the item as written would not necessarily violate the statement.
criteria.unclear: The item's wording leaves it genuinely open whether implementing it would violate the statement.

con-commitment-check.instructions: List to yourself the concrete commitments `item.text` makes. Does any of them rule out what `anchor.statement` requires, or require something the statement rules out, for a case the statement governs? Omission is not conflict, and commitments about cases outside the statement are not conflicts. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: At least one concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires for a case it governs.
criteria.no: No concrete commitment in the item rules out what the statement requires.
criteria.unclear: A commitment in the item might rule out the requirement, but it is too ambiguous to tell.
